record_scope_reconstruction: Short trucker protest affecting access to the Armenian Bagratashen road checkpoint opposite Sadakhlo on 15 September 2018. Customs’ spokesperson distinguishes the permitted protest from obstruction of customs work and reports clearance after roughly two to three hours. The reference locates the Armenian terminal; neither all lanes nor all passenger traffic are proven closed.

source_checks.finding: Customs spokesperson identifies the Bagratashen access protest, approximate duration and already reopened access.
Earlier newspaper account describes truckers’ grievances and threatened restrictions; it does not override the later customs qualification.
Official November 2016 inauguration identifies the new Bagratashen crossing facilities, predating the 2018 protest.
May 2018 Armenian terminal barrier coordinates independently inspected.
2018 position within a few metres of current terminal barrier.

sites.name: Bagratashen road checkpoint, Armenian side
sites.coordinate_method: Coordinates from explicitly versioned OSM node XML, independently compared with full node history
sites.precision: Approximate crossing area, about 100 m; not the historical barrier footprint
sites.evidence_note: The May 2018 node is a border-control barrier in the Armenian terminal lanes on the Alaverdi–Bagratashen M6/AH81 road. Current area XML connects these lanes to the named Bagratashen–Sadakhlo road bridge. The 2016 official inauguration establishes that this terminal predates the September 2018 episode. The Georgian Sadakhlo gate and later replacement bridge are not used as the obstruction location.

date_scope_check.finding: Geography review only. Current phase bounds, traffic exceptions, uncertain onset, reopening status and >24-hour decision are retained; current map features are not evidence of historical operation.
date_scope_check.qualification: REC50-R27-001-P1: The Armenian customs spokesperson reports a checkpoint-access blockage lasting about two to three hours from midnight on 15 September 2018, with the checkpoint open by the afternoon report. This does not qualify as longer than 24 hours. Customs permitted the protest and distinguished it from an intended obstruction of customs operations. No general passenger ban, all-lane customs shutdown or Georgian-truck-only rule is established. Exact minute timestamps, traffic cohorts and direction remain unknown.
